chapter: Breakup of Hines band to Lefty Bates
title: Vee-Jay house band with Lefty Bates
summary: Backed Jimmy Reed, John Lee Hooker, Jerry Butler.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Session players on the hits: "I played on that record"

blocks.x: (Recording interruption.)
Well, you did some recording with Jimmy Reed?
Yeah.
Did you do much blues work?
That's all we did.
Well, I mean besides with Jimmy?
Yeah, John Lee Hooker. And we did a lot of recordings, back-up, with the Spanials,, Jerry Butler. This was all when we was with VeeJay.
VeeJay?
Uh-huh.
Were you like the house bass player for Vee-Jay?
Yeah, like we was the house band.
Jimmy Reed's band?
Uh-huh.
Did you work --
No, Lefty Bates' Band.
Lefty Bates' Band?
Yeah.
And then Jimmy Reed would say, come in and --
Yeah, we was like the house band for We backed up all their artists.
Who else was in that house band? When was this, in the fifties?
Yeah.
Who else was in there?
It was different musicians from time to time, you know.
What was it, three or four man?

Like Lefty on guitar, piano player, Horace Palm and myself on bass, and who the heck was -- we had so many different drummers. Al Duncan, he was the main drummer, because he knew about this back beat.
That was all the go then. They'd record his back beat. Then it'd all depend on how many men they needed for the session. He'd hire extra men.
